cards.front: mixture
cards.back: Two or more substances mixed together but not joined. A mixture can be separated.
cards.say: mixture. Two or more substances mixed together but not joined. A mixture can be separated.

cards.front: sieving
cards.back: Using a sieve to separate big solid pieces from small ones, such as pebbles from sand.
cards.say: sieving. Using a sieve to separate big solid pieces from small ones, such as pebbles from sand.

cards.front: filtering
cards.back: Using filter paper to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.
cards.say: filtering. Using filter paper to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.

cards.front: residue
cards.back: The solid that is left behind on the filter paper.
cards.say: residue. The solid that is left behind on the filter paper.

cards.front: filtrate
cards.back: The liquid that passes through the filter paper.
cards.say: filtrate. The liquid that passes through the filter paper.

cards.front: magnetic separation
cards.back: Using a magnet to pick out magnetic materials, such as iron, from a mixture.
cards.say: magnetic separation. Using a magnet to pick out magnetic materials, such as iron, from a mixture.

cards.front: Which method separates iron nails from sand?
cards.back: Use a magnet. It picks up the iron nails and leaves the sand.
cards.say: Which method separates iron nails from sand? Use a magnet. It picks up the iron nails and leaves the sand.

cards.front: Which method separates sand from water?
cards.back: Filtering. The water passes through the paper and the sand stays behind.
cards.say: Which method separates sand from water? Filtering. The water passes through the paper and the sand stays behind.

cards.front: Which method gets salt from salty water?
cards.back: Evaporation. The water turns to vapour and the salt is left in the dish.
cards.say: Which method gets salt from salty water? Evaporation. The water turns to vapour and the salt is left in the dish.

cards.front: Which method separates rice from flour?
cards.back: Sieving. The flour passes through the holes and the rice grains stay in the sieve.
cards.say: Which method separates rice from flour? Sieving. The flour passes through the holes and the rice grains stay in the sieve.

cards.front: Does filtering separate dissolved salt from water?
cards.back: No. Dissolved particles are so tiny that they pass through the filter paper.
cards.say: Does filtering separate dissolved salt from water? No. Dissolved particles are so tiny that they pass through the filter paper.

cards.front: decanting
cards.back: Carefully pouring off a liquid from a solid that has settled at the bottom.
cards.say: decanting. Carefully pouring off a liquid from a solid that has settled at the bottom.

cards.front: sedimentation
cards.back: When heavier solid pieces settle to the bottom of a liquid.
cards.say: sedimentation. When heavier solid pieces settle to the bottom of a liquid.

cards.front: distillation
cards.back: Heating a solution so the liquid evaporates, then cooling the vapour so it condenses and is collected.
cards.say: distillation. Heating a solution so the liquid evaporates, then cooling the vapour so it condenses and is collected.

cards.front: Why does a coffee filter hold back the coffee grounds?
cards.back: The holes in the paper are too small for the grounds to pass through, but the liquid can.
cards.say: Why does a coffee filter hold back the coffee grounds? The holes in the paper are too small for the grounds to pass through, but the liquid can.

cards.front: What property of the pieces decides if sieving will work?
cards.back: Their size. The holes must let the small pieces through and stop the big ones.
cards.say: What property of the pieces decides if sieving will work? Their size. The holes must let the small pieces through and stop the big ones.

cards.front: How would you separate a mixture of sand, salt and iron filings?
cards.back: Use a magnet for the iron. Add water and filter out the sand. Evaporate the water to get the salt.
cards.say: How would you separate a mixture of sand, salt and iron filings? Use a magnet for the iron. Add water and filter out the sand. Evaporate the water to get the salt.

cards.front: Why can mixtures be separated easily?
cards.back: No new substance is made when they are mixed, so each substance keeps its own properties.
cards.say: Why can mixtures be separated easily? No new substance is made when they are mixed, so each substance keeps its own properties.

cards.front: Is salty water a mixture?
cards.back: Yes. It is a mixture of salt and water, and it is called a solution.
cards.say: Is salty water a mixture? Yes. It is a mixture of salt and water, and it is called a solution.

cards.front: How can a recycling centre pick out steel cans?
cards.back: It uses a strong magnet, because steel is magnetic.
cards.say: How can a recycling centre pick out steel cans? It uses a strong magnet, because steel is magnetic.

cards.front: How would you remove tea leaves from a cup of tea?
cards.back: Pour it through a strainer, which works like a sieve.
cards.say: How would you remove tea leaves from a cup of tea? Pour it through a strainer, which works like a sieve.
